items.reason: FLT_LOG_LEN (line 9) defines the length of flt_log ring buffer: static unsigned char flt_log[FLT_LOG_LEN]; used with mask (FLT_LOG_LEN - 1) for wraparound.
k_trip_a (line 13) is 'A rms, overload trip' and is compared in prot_slow: if (i_rms > k_trip_a) with action after ol_hold_ms. This is the software overload trip current (RMS).
ol_hold_ms (line 14) is the overload ride-through time; prot_slow increments ol_ms and trips only when ol_ms >= ol_hold_ms after i_rms exceeds k_trip_a.

Inline literal 21.2f in prot_fast (line 34) is commented 'peak of the RMS trip level' and triggers immediate inv_off and log_fault(FLT_OC) when abs(i_pk) exceeds it. This is a fast peak-current hardware-style software protection threshold.

Inline literal 0.9f in prot_slow (line 49) is used as vo_rms < 0.9f * VO_NOM to log a brownout fault (FLT_BRN). It defines the lower operating edge as a fraction of VO_NOM, not the trip level used for shutdown (no inv_off in this branch).
Inline literal 3 in prot_restart (line 54) is the retry limit: if (retry < 3) then delay_ms(500), inv_on().
Inline literal 500 in prot_restart (line 55) is the delay before retrying: delay_ms(500) prior to inv_on(). This is a restart backoff time, not the specified overload_delay.
FW_VER_MAJ (line 19) is the firmware major version ID.
VIN_LO_XFER (line 22) is the AC input window lower transfer point: “go to battery below this, Vrms” => lowest input voltage before transfer to battery.
VIN_HI_XFER (line 23) is the AC input window upper transfer point: “go to battery above this, Vrms” => highest input voltage before transfer to battery.
VBUS_REF (line 26) is labeled PFC regulation target, “V”. It corresponds to the DC bus regulation setpoint, rule vbus_set (though rule definition says bus minimum + margin, rounded up to 10 V).
VO_NOM (line 29) is output nominal voltage, Vrms. This is the intended output regulation setpoint (rule vout_set).
VO_TOL (line 30) is the tolerance band width given as ±0.03 around VO_NOM (ratio of nominal). It defines the regulation band edges indirectly, but is not itself a rule quantity.
VO_HI (line 31) is computed as VO_NOM * (1.0f + VO_TOL), i.e., upper edge of the output regulation band (+VO_TOL). Maps directly to rule vout_hi.
IO_RATED (line 32) is labeled “A rms, 1500 VA / 120 V” => rated output current (rule iout_rated).
I_TRIP_RMS (line 33) is labeled “overload shutdown, A rms” => software overload trip level (rule iout_trip).
TMR_LD (line 36) is labeled “PWM period, 25 kHz carrier” and is used as a PWM period register value. Maps to pwm_period in center-aligned count mode (TBPRD = f_clk/(2 f_sw)).
DB_CNT (line 37) is labeled “300 us dead time” and is the dead-time count register => pwm_deadband.
K_P (line 40) is labeled “voltage loop” proportional gain => vloop_kp.
K_I (line 41) is labeled “voltage loop” integral gain per control ISR => vloop_ki.
VBAT_NOM (line 44) is labeled “string nominal, V” => battery nominal voltage (vbat_nom).
VBAT_CUT (line 45) is labeled “end of discharge” => low-battery shutdown voltage (vbat_cutoff).
UART_BAUD (line 48) is the UART baud rate for front-panel/RS-232 port => comms_or_buffer.
PIN_BYP_RELAY (line 49) is a GPIO pin assignment for the static bypass relay drive => pin_map.
ADC_FULL (line 9) is the ADC full-scale count value for the sense chain (12-bit converter), used to derive per-count scaling (see K_VS).
DAC_FULL (line 10) is the comparator reference DAC full-scale code (used with CMP_DAC_HI/L0 to form hardware comparator trip thresholds).
VBUS_FS (line 13) is “V at ADC full scale” for the DC bus divider; it directly corresponds to the bus ADC full-scale voltage rule vbus_fs.
K_VS (line 14) is defined as (VBUS_FS / ADC_FULL) = volts per ADC count; corresponds to vbus_scale.
VBAT_FS (line 17) is “V at ADC full scale” for the battery divider; corresponds to vbat_fs.
VO_FS_PK (line 20) is “peak V at +/- half scale” for the output voltage mid-rail biased sense range; matches vout_fs_pk.
IO_FS_PK (line 23) is “peak A at +/- half scale” for mid-rail biased output current sensing; matches iout_fs_pk.
CMP_DAC_HI (line 24) is the positive overcurrent trip code from the comparator reference DAC; corresponds to iout_pklim_dac_hi.
CMP_DAC_LO (line 25) is (DAC_FULL - CMP_DAC_HI), the negative comparator trip code; corresponds to iout_pklim_dac_lo.
